text:
maria: quick heads-up — qwenx-lite int4 bring-up looks good on latency but we see a regression on summarization embedding similarity. baseline float sim ~0.92, int4 sim ~0.68 for the same prompt.

dev-bot: eval/job/1829999999 completed: task=summarization, metric=embed_cosine, baseline=0.923, qwenx-lite-int4=0.684, delta=-0.239 :warning:

sasha: ugh. did you run through the converter with the new rotary params? iirc qwenx-lite uses headwise rotary scale (0.75) in the ckpt metadata whereas our default runtime assumes 1.0.

maria: i suspected that. converter command used:```bash
python tools/convert_model.py \
  --src qwenx-lite/model.ckpt \
  --dst redwood/qwenx-lite-rlib \
  --quant int4 \
  --keep-rotary-meta \
```
but i also tried forcing rotary_scale=1.0 in the loader and the sim partially recovered to 0.79 (not back to 0.92).

jonathan: can you paste a minimal repro (inputs + postprocess) and a single example failing pair? also share tokenization diff if any. sometimes soft-hyphen or ZWJ changes token boundaries and that wrecks embedding comparisons.

maria: reproducible snippet:```python
from redwood_eval import load_model, embed
model = load_model('redwood/qwenx-lite-int4', rotary_scale=None) # None = use ckpt meta
prompt = 'Summarize: The committee voted unanimously to...'
ev = embed(model, prompt)
# saved outputs: before/after from float->int4 conversion
# example json: {"id":12,"cos_before":0.923,"cos_after":0.684}
```

eline: interestingly, tokenizer differences show soft-hyphen (U+00AD) being stripped in our normalization for qwenx, but kept in the original fan-provided tokenizer. that leads to different token sequences for ~1.2% of eval set.

sasha: that explains some percentage but not a 0.24 drop avg. we'll need to bisect: rotary params vs tokenizer vs quant kernel.

jonathan: suggested bisect plan:
1) run float model with our tokenizer+normalizer (to isolate tokenizer)
2) run int4 with rotary_scale overridden to original ckpt value (to isolate rotary)
3) run int4 with alternative quant kernel (we have two int4 kernels: fast vs stable)

maria: results so far:
- float + our-tokenizer => avg cos 0.915 (small loss from tokenization only)
- float + ckpt-tokenizer => 0.923 (baseline)
- int4 + ckpt-tokenizer + rotary_scale=1.0 => 0.791
- int4 + ckpt-tokenizer + rotary_scale=0.75 => 0.684 (current)
- int4 (stable-kernel) + ckpt-tokenizer + rotary_scale=0.75 => 0.695

dev-bot: note: quant-kernel differences logged at infra/quant-kernel/fast_vs_stable/1829999999

sasha: those numbers point to a combined effect: rotary_scale mismatch moves things ~0.10 and quant-kernel + other numeric error ~0.05-0.1.

jonathan: next steps: we should try an explicit per-head rotary rescale shim in runtime (apply scale correction to cached kv rotations) and re-eval. if that recovers to >0.9 we can add automatic shim for models that declare non-standard rotary metadata.

maria: i can prototype shim this afternoon. quick patch:```diff
--- a/runtime/rotary.cu
+++ b/runtime/rotary.cu
@@
-    apply_rotary(q, k, rotary_scale=1.0);
+    apply_rotary(q, k, rotary_scale=model.rotary_meta.scale); // fallback to 1.0 if missing
```

eline: also opened a small PR to normalize soft-hyphen handling to match qwenx tokenizer behavior: redwood/docs#2781. linking tests in the PR.

sasha: action items: @maria prototype rotary shim + run quick eval subset (n=500), @eline land tokenizer normalization test, @jonathan add quant-kernel stress tests to CI.

maria: will post results here once shim run finishes (kicking off now).

dev-bot: job/1830000050 started: qwenx-lite-int4-rotary-shim-smoke, subset=500

jonathan: thanks — if shim recovers most of the loss, we should add an onboarding lint that warns when ckpt rotary != runtime default. prevents future surprises. :+1:

maria: quick update: shim run finished, partial recovery to avg cos 0.88 on subset. will run full eval tomorrow. creating a follow-up issue with logs and diffs.

sasha: great, that indicates safe path: shim + kernel tuning + tokenizer normalization. good triage.

maria: filing issue now: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RI-12345 with logs and repro.

eline: thanks all — keeping this thread as the single source of truth for the onboarding triage.
